title: Scout (trace-callers, capped rerun of T-0009): readers of the codex model, tier map, fallback_tier; slots for [[executors]]
spec:
HARD OUTPUT CAP: your entire JSON result must be under 4,500 characters or it is dropped by the bus (T-0009 was lost this way). At most 12 findings; each claim ≤160 chars; evidence = path:line strings only, no code quotes; no summary prose beyond 300 chars.
Skill trace-callers. Trace every reader of: pool.cfg["codex"] keys (model, max_parallel, daily_budget_tasks, pace_reserve, on_exhausted, dangerous_full_access), pool.cfg["models"], fallback_tier(), Pool.codex_available(), Pool.codex state (cooldown_until, day_tasks, running), the `-m` arg in executor._run/start/reply, bus.log_run tier/account. Then in suggested_next (≤5 items, ≤200 chars each) name, in blast-radius order, where a pool.toml `[[executors]]` table (id, provider codex|claude, model, max_parallel, daily_budget_tasks, roles, complexity_min/max, enabled, quota_group) would plug in: the function that picks an executor by (role, complexity, health), where per-executor cooldown state goes in pool_state.json, how run logs carry executor id. List tests in tests/test_orchestrator.py that read these fields.
acceptance: result JSON under 4,500 chars and posted to the bus
suggested_next lists insertion points in blast-radius order

result.summary: Posted result for T-0012, status done. 12 findings, all with path:line evidence, under the 4,500-char cap. Suggested_next lists 5 insertion points for `[[executors]]` in blast-radius order: Pool.codex_available/Codex dataclass → Pool.pick(role) → pool_state.json keying → model/-m resolution in executor.py/spawn.py → log_run executor id.

findings.claim: executor.start builds codex -m arg from pool.cfg[codex].model, gpt-6-astra default
Pool.codex_available reads cfg[codex].max_parallel and daily_budget_tasks to gate dispatch
executor._run/_exhausted read on_exhausted policy to pick fallback tier or hold
executor.py builds --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox from cfg.dangerous_full_access, else workspace-write
pace_reserve key has zero readers in repo (dead/unused config key)
spawn.run_worker reads pool.cfg[models][tier] to pick Claude model per task tier
fallback_tier(complexity) maps <=5 sonnet, 6-8 opus, >=9 None(hold); called by executor and mcp
Codex dataclass fields cooldown_until/day_tasks/running mutated in executor.py and read in pool.status/codex_available
bus.log_run(tier=,account=) called from executor.py (codex, tier astra) and spawn.py (claude, tier/account per task)
Pool.pick(role) is the sole existing account-selection function, keyed on role+utilization, no complexity/health-by-executor concept yet
Pool state persists to pool_state.json via Pool.save/_load, keyed by account id; codex has one implicit singleton, not per-executor
mcp.py status() and cli.py expose pool.status() incl codex.on_exhausted/running/day_tasks to callers

open_questions: Is pace_reserve planned but unimplemented, or a stale key from an older config schema?
suggested_next: 1. orchestrator/pool.py:107 Pool.codex_available/Codex dataclass - replace singleton codex state with per-executor-id entries
2. orchestrator/pool.py:76 Pool.pick(role) - extend selection to (role,complexity,health) across [[executors]], not just role+affinity
3. orchestrator/pool.py:63 PERSIST/pool_state.json - key cooldown/day_tasks/running by executor id instead of accounts/codex split
4. orchestrator/executor.py:81 and spawn.py:124 - resolve model/-m arg from [[executors]].model instead of cfg[codex]/cfg[models][tier]
5. orchestrator/bus.py:100 log_run + spawn.py:92,101/executor.py:58,61 - add executor id field alongside tier/account in run logs
